alignment.note: Greek uses relative pronoun ὃς with explanatory particle γάρ ('for whoever'); Peshitta employs indefinite relative ܡܢ ('whoever'); Vulgate uses compound indefinite Quisquis with enim ('for'), mirroring Greek structure more closely than Syriac.

Greek and Peshitta attest the negative construction 'who is not against us' (οὐκ ἔστιν καθ᾽ ἡμῶν / ܕܠܐ ܗܘܐ ܠܘܩܒܠܟܘܢ). The Vulgate transmits an entirely different verse (Mark 9:41, the cup-of-water saying), indicating either a manuscript tradition conflating verses or a scribal error in the provided Vulgate tokens.

Vulgate includes the complete text of Mark 9:41 ('Whoever gives you a cup of water in my name, because you are Christ's, amen I say to you, he will not lose his reward'), which is absent from both Greek and Peshitta witnesses for this verse (Mark 9:40). This represents either a versification discrepancy or textual corruption in the supplied Vulgate data.
